text:
sara: heads-up — customer BrightByte opened a P1: their app pods in prod VPC can't resolve the service endpoint for collector.bb.prod.svc (NXDOMAIN from node-local), but curl from their bastion to the same name works. Case 987654.

 darren_support: thanks — any recent infra changes on their account or VPC? route53 hosted zone changes, resolver rules, or shared hosted-zones?

 sara: they migrated some infra last night (moved a subnet to a new AZ), but they say no Route53 edits. forwarding rules look new-ish in their AWS Console: a resolver rule that forwards *.bb.prod.svc to 10.10.10.5 (their on-prem DNS).

 ryan_netops: forwarding to on-prem is suspicious. node-local (169.254.20.10) is returning NXDOMAIN, you said bastion resolves — do you have dig outputs?

 sara: pasted logs from their pod: 

 ```
$ kubectl exec -n prod svc-collector-5b9f -- nslookup collector.bb.prod.svc
Server: 169.254.20.10
Address: 169.254.20.10#53
*** No DNS name

$ dig @169.254.20.10 collector.bb.prod.svc +short

$ dig @172.31.6.2 collector.bb.prod.svc +short
10.2.3.45

$ dig @10.0.0.10 collector.bb.prod.svc +short
10.2.3.45
```

 bastion dig against 172.31.6.2 (VPC resolver) returns the A. node-local returns nothing.

 jess: are kube-proxy / coredns stubDomains configured to forward that suffix anywhere? node-local sometimes rewrites stub domains and prefers local cache.

 sara: they have node-local-dns on nodes (iptables redirect to 169.254.20.10). coredns configmap in cluster shows: 

 ```yaml
stubDomains:
  "bb.prod.svc": ["169.254.20.10"]
```

 ryan_netops: aha. So node-local is forwarding bb.prod.svc to 169.254.20.10 which is itself node-local — loop? but their resolver rule forwards bb.prod.svc to on-prem 10.10.10.5. If the on-prem DNS doesn't have the private hosted zone data it will return NXDOMAIN. Bastion query to VPC resolver may have hit a different resolver rule path that resolves via Route53 private zone. Need to confirm VPC resolver rule priorities and which rule their bastion uses.

 darren_support: quick repro suggestion for them: from a node run 

 ```sh
# nslookup using sysresolv (bypass node-local iptables)
kubectl debug -n prod node/$NODE --image=busybox -- nslookup collector.bb.prod.svc 172.31.6.2
```

 sara: they ran something similar — querying 172.31.6.2 succeeded. querying node-local ip returned NXDOMAIN.

 jess: check Route53 private hosted zone association: if the private hosted zone for bb.prod.svc is associated to the VPC but the new resolver rule for the VPC is forwarding that suffix to on-prem, Route53 won't be consulted. Essentially the resolver rule (outbound forward) wins over the hosted zone for queries coming from node-local if the node-local resolver is configured to follow the rule.

 ryan_netops: also ask them to check the resolver rule association scope (account vs cross-account). I’ve seen customers create a forwarding rule accidentally in the same VPC that routes to an empty on-prem zone.

 infrabot: deploy-bot noticed recent change: resolver rule rr-ff12 added 2026-03-10 by iam:brightbyte-netops, target 10.10.10.5, pattern "bb.prod.svc."

 darren_support: suggests steps for BrightByte: 1) temp remove the forwarder rule or set its priority lower; 2) or update on-prem DNS to include records or forward unknown to AWS; 3) change node-local stubDomains to query 172.31.6.2 directly instead of 169.254.20.10.

 sara: customer tried removing the resolver rule in AWS console and node-local queries started resolving immediately. Their team says they added the rule for a different suffix and typo'd the domain.

 jess: good catch. we should advise: - add a short verification checklist for customers before adding resolver rules (confirm trailing dot, correct suffix, test with dig against 172.31.6.2) - recommend using Route53 Resolver query logs to validate which resolver handled queries.

 ryan_netops: noted. also file a small KB in support: common pitfall — forwarder rules shadowing Route53 private hosted zones (typos on suffixes). include how node-local can make the issue look like an in-cluster DNS failure because the node-local IP returns NXDOMAIN.

 sara: I'll update case 987654 with the resolution steps and the recommendation to add a resolver-rule naming review. closing once customer confirms prod traffic is green. :white_check_mark:

 darren_support: thx all :thumbsup:
